Question Choices: How many 3-card hands can be chosen from 8 distinct cards?
Solution: Choose 3 distinct members from 8; order does not matter, so use C(8,3)=8!/[3!(5)!]=56. Dividing by the number of orders of each selected group avoids duplicate counts.

Question Choices: A class has 5 girls and 4 boys. How many 3-person groups contain exactly 2 girls?
Solution: Choose exactly 2 of the 5 girls in C(5,2)=10 ways and 1 of the 4 boys in C(4,1)=4 ways. Each first choice pairs with every second choice, so multiply to get 40 groups. Choosing from the whole class without restrictions would include wrong compositions.

Question Choices: If exactly one of 36 equally likely combinations wins what is the winning probability?
Solution: Exactly one of 36 equally likely outcomes wins. Thus P(win)=1/36=1/36. Count combinations as outcomes because their equal probabilities are stated.
